name: TamperLog
description: If someone edits the audit trail, the audit trail should tell you. That was the idea behind my graduation project.
problem: An audit log is only useful if you can trust it. I wanted to explore how to detect changes to earlier records instead of relying on the log server alone.
built: I built a prototype that links log entries with SHA-256 hashes and checks them against distributed checkpoints. It combines a Flask backend with a JavaScript interface and explores threshold signatures for checkpoint verification.
learned: The interesting part was the trust model: what gets detected, who can verify a checkpoint, and what happens when one component is no longer trustworthy.
status: Graduation project prototype. The implementation and trust model are research work, not a production security guarantee.
previewCaption: Me, explaining why a log should be able to tell on itself.

name: GRC AI
description: A team project exploring whether local AI can make policy reviews less painful.
problem: Reviewing policies against several compliance frameworks involves a lot of reading, cross-referencing, and handling documents that may be sensitive.
built: I led a team building a prototype that uses local AI to analyze policy documents against multiple compliance frameworks. We used Ollama and Gemma 2 2B to explore the workflow without relying on a hosted model.
learned: The useful question was where AI could support a review and where a person still needed to make the decision. A model's answer is a starting point, not proof of compliance.
status: Hackathon prototype; the team placed in the national top five.
evidenceAlt: Presenting the GRC AI team project

name: LocalLLM
description: A small Flask interface for Ollama. Run a model on your own machine, open your browser, and start talking.
problem: I wanted a straightforward way to use local language models without making every conversation someone else's data.
built: I made a Flask web interface for running Ollama models locally. Once a model is downloaded, the application can run offline.
learned: Making local AI approachable means paying attention to the setup and the interface, as well as the model. Open source also gives other people a way to inspect and improve that work.
status: Open-source project. Hardware requirements and behavior depend on the model you choose.
evidenceAlt: The merged pull request adding LocalLLM to Ollama's community integrations
imageAlt: The LocalLLM community integration pull request on Ollama

name: GRC Check
description: Work through a privacy and security self-assessment without sending your answers to a server.
problem: Compliance frameworks can be difficult to work through, especially when the answers describe how an organization handles sensitive data.
built: I built a local-first self-assessment around Jordan's data protection law and ISO 27001. The tool keeps the answers on the device.
learned: The challenge was turning long requirements into questions someone could actually work through, while keeping their answers private.
status: A self-assessment tool to help organize your thinking. It does not certify compliance or replace a professional assessment.
